aspect: Both too much and too little are named in law
description: Japan's labour ministry panel listed assigning impossible tasks and giving an employee little or no work among the six constituent acts of power harassment. The 2019 statute turns on conduct exceeding what is necessary and appropriate for the business.
energy_note: Named in statute, in at least one country.

description: The missed deadline is real and documented. The reason it was missed is not documented anywhere, because nobody minutes the withholding of information.
energy_note: The failure is on file. The cause is not.

description: 'Client's expecting the model Monday morning.' It is 17:40 on Friday. The data access request he was asked to approve on Tuesday is still sitting unapproved in his queue. On Monday, in front of the team: 'We had a slip on this one. Let's make sure it doesn't repeat.'
energy_note: Set up on Friday, corrected in public on Monday.

aspect: Being given nothing is harder to report
description: An empty calendar is not an incident. The target cannot point to an act, and the isolation is visible to colleagues as evidence that something must be wrong with them.
energy_note: Nothing happened to you, for eleven weeks.

aspect: It converts into a lawful dismissal
description: After two review cycles the file supports a capability process that is, on its own documents, entirely fair.
energy_note: Dismissed fairly, on a record that was constructed.
